study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Yu et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2024
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Behavioral and brain morphological changes before and after hemispherotomy

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The normative model was built using 11 MRI datasets of healthy children (2115 total after QC). Five of these match the standard dataset list: ABIDE-I (168 post-QC), ABIDE-II (332 post-QC), devCCNP (referred to as CCNP in the paper; 116 post-QC), HBN (76 post-QC), and HCP-D (referred to as HCPD; 252 post-QC). Six additional datasets are not in the standard list: UNC/UMN Baby Connectome Project (BCP; 257 post-QC), Calgary Preschool MRI Dataset (CPMD; 90 post-QC), Children School Functions and Brain Development Project (CBD; 69 post-QC), Infant Brain Imaging Study (IBIS; 183 post-QC), Multicenter Database on Perinatal Factors in Child Brain-Mind Development (PeriCBD; 43 post-QC), Pediatric Imaging Neurocognition and Genetics (PING; 415 post-QC), and Pixar Dataset (114 post-QC). The patient data (29 left and 28 right hemispherotomy) were acquired at a single site (Peking University First Hospital), coded as SINGLE-SITE.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "the healthy subjects used for normative model estimation were from 11 MRI datasets, including the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange ... the UNC/UMN Baby Connectome Project ... the Calgary Preschool MRI Dataset ... the Children School Functions and Brain Development Project ... the Chinese Color Nest Project ... the Healthy Brain Network ... the Human Connectome Project-Development ... the Infant Brain Imaging Study ... the Multicenter Database on Perinatal Factors in Child Brain-Mind Development ... the Pediatric Imaging, Neurocognition, and Genetics ... and the Pixar Dataset" ; "underwent peri-insular hemispherotomy between 2016 and 2021 at the Pediatric Epilepsy Center, Peking University First Hospital"

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: All 11 datasets of healthy children (including the 5 listed above plus 6 not in the standard list: BCP, CPMD, CBD, IBIS, PeriCBD, PING, Pixar) were used as training data for the Gaussian process regression normative model. The patient data from Peking University First Hospital were used as test data for the normative model to derive individual Z-scores, which were then analyzed for pre- vs. post-surgery GMV changes.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "The GMV images of the 2115 healthy children and our pediatric hemispherotomy patients were used as the training and testing data, respectively. Age and sex were included as covariates in the model. For each voxel, Gaussian process regression was applied to predict each patient's GMV, yielding a Z score representing the patient's derivation from the age- and sex-matched healthy norm."

model-1.model-name: voxelwise GMV normative model (Gaussian process regression)

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model was built for voxelwise GMV using Gaussian process regression via PCNtoolkit. All 2115 healthy children served as training data. There was no separate validation/test split within the healthy cohort; the patients were used as test data. Initially 2343 children were selected (age 0.3-13.0 years, max 100 per half-year interval from 11 datasets), but 228 were excluded due to poor image quality or processing failure.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "we included T1-weighted images from all healthy children aged between 0.3 and 13.0 years across these datasets, with a maximum of 100 subjects for a half-year interval (in total 2343 children)" ... "228 were excluded due to poor image quality or image processing failure. VBM processing was then applied to the remaining 2115 children" ... "The GMV images of the 2115 healthy children and our pediatric hemispherotomy patients were used as the training and testing data, respectively."

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The overall and train phases are the same since all 2115 healthy children were used for training. The paper specifies the inclusion age range as 0.3-13.0 years but does not report mean, SD, median, or IQR for the healthy reference cohort. Supplementary Table S1 provides age ranges per dataset but not per-dataset means/SDs for the included healthy children, so weighted mean and pooled SD cannot be computed.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "we included T1-weighted images from all healthy children aged between 0.3 and 13.0 years across these datasets, with a maximum of 100 subjects for a half-year interval (in total 2343 children)"

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The paper states that age and sex were included as covariates in the normative model, but does not report the sex distribution (male/female counts or percentages) for the 2115 healthy children used in the reference cohort. Supplementary Table S1 provides subject numbers per dataset but not sex breakdowns.
